Cycle to Zero

May 21–23, 2027

Friday, May 21 through Sunday, May 23, 2027. The 1-day ride is Saturday, May 22. The first ride was May 29–31, 2026.

Sign up for Cycle to Zero Official site (sfaf.org)

05.21 San Francisco

What is the Cycle to Zero?

Cycle to Zero is San Francisco AIDS Foundation’s three-day ride from San Francisco to the Russian River and back. In 2027 it runs May 21–23: about 85 miles north through Marin to Guerneville, a day of riding from camp or a day off, then about 85 miles home down the Sonoma coast. Registration is $95 and the fundraising minimum is $2,500 for 3-day cyclists. Riders camp both nights in Guerneville.

How Cycle to Zero started

AIDS/LifeCycle ran from San Francisco to Los Angeles for seven days every June and ended in 2025. San Francisco AIDS Foundation, one of its two producers, announced Cycle to Zero in September 2025 as a three-day ride that builds on that history.

The first Cycle to Zero was May 29–31, 2026, north to Guerneville and back. The name is the foundation’s goal: zero new HIV diagnoses, zero stigma, zero inequity, zero overdose.

What to expect on the day

Day 1 goes north from San Francisco through Marin County, past redwood forests, to Guerneville on the Russian River. It’s about 85 miles.

Day 2 is yours. Let’s Chill is about 40 miles and the Zero-Hero Century is about 100, both from Guerneville. You can also skip the bike for the foundation’s activities or a day in town.

Camp is at Camp Russian River and Johnson’s Beach in Guerneville, about a 15-minute walk apart, both nights. For 3-day cyclists the ride is fully supported, with all meals and camping included. Day 3 is about 85 miles back to San Francisco by the Sonoma coast.

The town guide

Ride, sleep, eat, fix the bike.

San Francisco is a city you ride out of without a car. Over the Golden Gate Bridge to the Marin Headlands and Mt. Tamalpais; along the ocean on Sunset Dunes, the old Great Highway, now closed to cars; by BART to the Berkeley hills and by Caltrain to the Peninsula climbs; home from Marin on the ferry. The bridge is open to bikes around the clock. Alaska, Delta and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026); one North Beach shop builds a shipped bike; two city shops rent carbon road and gravel bikes from $100 a day. Bring yours for three days or more.

Fly into SFO (about 11 miles south of City Hall) or Oakland (about 12 miles, across the bay; the door for the East Bay hills). San José is 39 miles out, a fallback fare. From SFO, BART runs from the International Terminal into the city and takes bikes. The airport has bike assembly stands, so you can build the bike there and ride the train in. From Oakland, BART is across the street from the terminals. You don’t need a car. The bridge, the Headlands and Golden Gate Park start in the city. BART reaches the Berkeley hills, Caltrain the Peninsula, and the Golden Gate ferries bring you home from Sausalito, Tiburon and Larkspur. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the shop that builds a shipped bike, and each transit agency’s bike rules.

Cycle to Zero FAQ

When is Cycle to Zero in 2027?

May 21–23, 2027, a Friday through a Sunday. The 1-day ride is Saturday, May 22.

What is the Cycle to Zero route?

Day 1 is San Francisco to Guerneville, about 85 miles north through Marin County past redwood forests. Day 2 starts and ends in Guerneville: about 40 miles or about 100, or a day off. Day 3 is about 85 miles back to San Francisco by the Sonoma coast.

What is the fundraising minimum?

$2,500 for 3-day cyclists, due by May 1, 2027, with a $95 registration fee. 1-day cyclists pay $225 and have no minimum. Crew volunteers pay $95 and raise at least $250.

Where do riders sleep?

In camp in Guerneville, both nights, at Camp Russian River and Johnson’s Beach. The two are about a 15-minute walk apart. Camping is included for 3-day cyclists.

Can I ride just one day?

Yes. 1-day cyclists ride Day 2, Saturday, May 22, from Guerneville. Registration is $225 and there is no fundraising minimum.

Where does the money go?

To the programs and services of San Francisco AIDS Foundation.
